shortDescription: Uganda plans to cut its public spending in the 2027/28 (July-June) financial year by 6.2% as it scales back borrowing, the finance ministry said on Friday.

children: Uganda plans to cut its public spending in the 2027/28 (July-June) financial year by 6.2% as it scales back borrowing, the finance ministry said on Friday.
The East African country plans to spend 79.2 trillion Ugandan shillings ($20.1 billion) in the 12 months starting next July, down from 84.4 trillion, the ministry said a statement posted on X.
The lower spending reflects "reduced reliance on borrowing and external financing, and allocative efficiency", the ministry said. It did not give details of the planned cut in borrowing.
Uganda has been trying to trim its growing public debt and cut the cost of repayments, which the central bank says are eating into resources needed for spending on health and education.

Economic growth in the 2027/28 financial year is projected at 9.1%, up from a revised forecast of 7.6% in the previous period, "driven by the onset of commercial production of oil and gas", the ministry said.
Uganda hopes to commence oil exports early next year from fields in its west operated by France's TotalEnergies
and state-owned Uganda National Oil Company (UNOC).
In 2027/28, resources will be funnelled into priority areas including agro-industrialisation, tourism and mineral development, including oil and gas, the ministry said.
